conventions: mul penei rendered by a single English front (8.2, 8.3) is one fused unit under rule 30, headed on mul, and penei is not marked unrepresented: rule 22 reaches a repetition of the same element, not the parts of an idiom. What is spent on the pair is one word only, since the in belongs to el and the of to the nomen rectum under rule 19. Heading on penei, as the chapter's six lifnei units do, was the competing reading.

la'avod 'eth is aligned two ways in this chapter and the difference is in the Hebrew, not in the analysis. Where the Hebrew writes 'avodah (8.11, 8.19, 8.22) the infinitive takes do, the noun takes the service, and the object marker is unrepresented; at 8.15 no 'avodah is written, so do the service is the light verb's whole rendering of 'avad (rule 44) and the object marker takes the of through which it reaches 'ohel mo'ed (rule 16). 8.26's sheret 'eth 'echaw -> minister with their brethren is the same reading of the marker. Do not level these into one treatment.

li rendered by a single mine (8.14 shall be mine, 8.17 are mine) is one fused unit of preposition and suffix under rule 30, on the reasoning rule 22 gives for bah -> therein: the one English word carries both the relation and the pronoun. The lamed is not marked unrepresented under rule 40, which governs a recasting that leaves the preposition nothing to say, and here nothing is left over.
report: Checked all 41 candidate groups. Every multi-treatment bucket but one is the ASV writing different English for the same morpheme, and the difference is licensed by what is written. The object marker takes 'of' at 8.15 and 'with' at 8.26 because there the English predicate reaches its object through a supplied preposition, while 8.11, 8.19 and 8.22 write the object noun bare: 8.15's Hebrew has no 'avodah at all, so 'the service' is the light verb's complement and the 'of' is the marker's under rules 16 and 44. kol takes 'the whole' at 8.9 and 'all' at 8.20 because the single written 'the' stands before a different word in each (rule 29). The age idiom gives ben 'old' at 8.24 and 'the age' at 8.25. hayah has three ASV frames (8.11 'it may be', 8.14 'shall be', 8.19 existential 'there be'). The lamed before an infinitive is unrepresented only in the three lemor verses (rule 27) and takes the written 'to' everywhere else.

The one genuine error is mul penei at 8.2 and 8.3. Both verses aligned mul to 'front' and marked penei unrepresented under rule 22. Rule 22 governs a repetition of the same element, and rule 30 says so in terms: 'Rule 22 governs a repetition of the same element, not the parts of an idiom.' By each verse's own alignment the 'in' is el's and the 'of' is the rectum's, so exactly one English word, 'front', is spent on the pair; rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the two morphemes share one unit, exactly as the chapter's own six lifnei -> 'before' units already do. Patched both verses, headed on mul, whose lexeme 'front' writes, with the competing penei head named in the note.

BSB: 16 disagreements, and only the two penei tokens at 8.2 and 8.3 are a genuine error. The patch agrees with BSB there, but it is carried by rule 30 and not by the comparison. The rest stand as documented convention differences: seven object markers (rule 16), the lamed of lemor (rule 27), the paragogic he of wa'ettenah at 8.19 (rule 32), the two recast min's at 8.16 and 8.25 (rules 19 and 40), and the two assimilated-article bet's of 'both man and beast' at 8.17, for which the ASV writes no preposition at all (rule 40). No accepted edge was moved to improve the rate.

The table is blind to added units, so I read the dump for supplied English folded into a neighbour. The four added units (8.3 'so as to give light', 8.4 the 'and' between two 'ad phrases, 8.11 'theirs', 8.16 appositional 'even') each answer to no morpheme, and nothing comparable is folded elsewhere: 8.24's two 'and's both have waws written for them, 8.17's correlative 'both ... and' is one waw's pair, and the chapter writes no second appositional 'even' or supplied possessive.

Left uniform and not disturbed: bekor -> 'the first born' heads on 'born' in all four units (8.16, 8.17 twice, 8.18). Rule 31's tie procedure would also support heading on 'first', since the ASV never writes 'born' alone for the word, but the chapter is internally uniform and the notes name the tie, so this is a head preference and not a split. Recorded here rather than patched.

Also checked and left: the chapter uses status 'aligned' for every rule 30 fusion (lifnei six times, ka-asher twice, ben baqar twice, me-eth, li -> 'mine', ma'lah), which the corpus permits alongside noncompositional for the same expressions; the two new mul penei units follow that chapter practice.
